summary: Places UI Kit is the decisive finding: Google Maps Platform Service Specific Terms section 15.1 (last modified June 10, 2026) explicitly permits it "with or without any map, including a non-Google Map" and states this "will prevail over the No Use with Non-Google Maps clause" — so the marketing claim is confirmed by the actual contract, including for reviews. It bills flat per component instantiation regardless of fields returned, at 10,000 free calls/SKU/month then $1.00/1,000. Conversely, section 14.2 flatly bans raw Places API content "in conjunction with a non-Google map", which the current businessfind plan (server.js proxy JSON on a MapLibre/Leaflet map) would violate. Separately, the field masks already in server.js put nearby search on the Enterprise SKU and place details on Enterprise+Atmosphere, so the configured daily caps imply roughly $615/month rather than a free app. All 12 hardcoded place type strings are valid Table A types, so there is no silent zero-results bug there. The $200 monthly credit ended March 1, 2025 and was replaced with per-SKU free tiers of 10K Essentials / 5K Pro / 1K Enterprise calls per month.

findings.topic: BLOCKER — Places API content may NOT be shown with a non-Google map (ToS 14.2)
findings.detail: Google Maps Platform Service Specific Terms (last modified June 10, 2026), Section 14, verbatim: "14. Places API (Legacy and New) — 14.1 Use without a Google Map. Customer may use Google Maps Content from the Places API in Customer Applications without a corresponding Google Map. 14.2 No use with a non-Google map. Customer must not use Google Maps Content from the Places API in conjunction with a non-Google map. 14.3 Caching. Customer may temporarily cache latitude and longitude values from the Places API for up to 30 consecutive calendar days, after which Customer must delete the cached latitude and longitude values." Implication for businessfind: the current architecture (server.js proxying places:searchNearby, then plotting pins on a map) is compliant only if the map is a Google map. MapLibre/Leaflet plus /api/nearby pins is a terms violation. A list-only view with no map at all IS allowed under 14.1.

findings.topic: Places UI Kit — explicitly permitted on a non-Google map, and it overrides 14.2
findings.detail: Same terms document, Section 15, verbatim: "15. Places UI Kit — 15.1 Places UI Kit usage. Customer may use Places UI Kit in Customer Applications with or without any map, including a non-Google Map. This clause will prevail over the No Use with Non-Google Maps clause of the Agreement. 15.2 Caching. Customer may temporarily cache latitude and longitude values from the Places UI Kit for up to 30 consecutive calendar days, after which Customer must delete the cached latitude and longitude values. 15.3 Use of Third-party products. To the extent that Customer uses Places UI Kit with third-party products or services in its Customer Application, Customer does so at its own discretion. Customer is responsible for (a) compliance with any applicable laws, regulations, industry standards or other requirements; (b) any misalignment that may arise from such use; and (c) ensuring that any use with a third-party service is compliant [with the restrictions] against caching and exporting Google Maps Content and creating content from Google Maps Content; and (d) complying with Google's attribution requirements including making it clear to the End User what is Google Maps Content and what content is not from Google. 15.4 No Alteration of Google Attribution, Links, or Notices. Customer may not remove, alter, or obscure Google provided attribution, links to terms, or user-facing notices." Google's marketing claim is therefore CONFIRMED by the contract — but only for content rendered by the UI Kit components themselves, not for raw Places API JSON fetched server-side and rendered in your own HTML. Reviews inside a UI Kit Place Details element on a MapLibre map: allowed. Reviews pulled via /api/place and rendered in your own card next to a MapLibre map: not allowed.

findings.topic: Places UI Kit — flat-rate billing regardless of fields (CONFIRMED)
findings.detail: developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/places-ui-kit/overview, verbatim: "Places UI Kit queries are billed per component instantiation, not based on the Places API data included in the response." A Place Details element showing reviews, photos, hours and ratings therefore costs the same as one showing only a name. Components: Place Details Elements, Advanced Place Details Elements (preview), Place Search Elements, Advanced Place Search Elements (preview), Advanced Place List Element (preview), Basic Place Autocomplete Element. The Maps JS usage-and-billing page states requests from Place Details and Place Search elements bill to the Places UI Kit Query SKU, Autocomplete bills to the per-session SKU, and "underlying requests to the Places API and Geocoding API don't consume quota on your Cloud project." Rate limit 6,000 queries/minute/project for Place Details and Place Search elements. Places UI Kit reached GA on July 16, 2025.

findings.topic: Places UI Kit free allowance — 10,000 free calls per SKU per month
findings.detail: Google Maps Platform core services pricing list: Places UI Kit Query (SKU 0678-4F72-DA7C) 10,000 free/month, then $1.00 per 1,000 at tier 1 scaling to $0.08 per 1,000 at high volume. Places UI Kit — Autocomplete Per Session (924B-2797-26F1) 10,000 free/month, $10.00 down to $0.80 per 1,000. Places UI Kit Pro (42AB-1FB3-B56A) 5,000 free/month, $5.00 down to $0.38 per 1,000. I could not confirm from official docs exactly which components bill to the Pro SKU — most likely the Advanced (preview) elements. Verify before relying on it.

Format: SKU — free calls/month — tier-1 price per 1,000 down to lowest volume-discount price per 1,000. NEARBY SEARCH: Pro (99F9-A108-83A6) 5,000 free, $32.00 to $2.40. Enterprise (772E-9975-BE34) 1,000 free, $35.00 to $2.63. Enterprise + Atmosphere (F20E-7034-0EF7) 1,000 free, $40.00 to $3.40. There is NO Nearby Search Essentials SKU — Pro is the floor. PLACE DETAILS: Essentials (6E05-E1C3-8D85) 10,000 free, $5.00 to $0.38. Pro (4ED6-464A-2AFC) 5,000 free, $17.00 to $1.28. Enterprise (2D9A-3DE0-3766) 1,000 free, $20.00 to $1.51. Enterprise + Atmosphere (EB23-5ECC-F753) 1,000 free, $25.00 to $2.28. Place Details Photos (DCD1-FE97-8C71) 1,000 free, $7.00 to $0.53. OTHER: Dynamic Maps / Maps JavaScript map loads (FAF4-3B2D-51B2) 10,000 free, $7.00 to $0.53. Geocoding (BAC8-4E68-E261) 10,000 free, $5.00 to $0.38. These were read off the official page via a summarising fetch — reconfirm exact figures before quoting them externally.

findings.topic: Free tier: the $200/month credit is gone, replaced March 1, 2025
findings.detail: Per developers.google.com/maps/billing-and-pricing/march-2025 and the billing FAQ: effective March 1, 2025 the universal USD $200 monthly credit was replaced with per-SKU free monthly call allowances scaled by tier — 10,000 free calls per SKU per month for Essentials, 5,000 for Pro, 1,000 for Enterprise (Essentials Map Tiles gets 100,000). Google's worked example: a project using 10,000 Geocoding plus 5,000 Text Search Pro calls paid $10/month under the old credit and pays $0 under the new scheme. Because the allowance is per SKU, a narrow app using few SKUs usually benefits; an app leaning on one Enterprise SKU is much worse off.

findings.topic: COST ALARM — the caps in .env.example imply roughly $615/month, not a free app
findings.detail: server.js sends X-Goog-FieldMask 'places.id,places.displayName,places.location,places.rating,places.userRatingCount,places.priceLevel,places.primaryType,places.businessStatus' on searchNearby. rating, userRatingCount and priceLevel are Enterprise-tier fields, so every nearby search bills at Nearby Search ENTERPRISE: $35/1,000 with only 1,000 free/month. NEARBY_DAILY_CAP=500 gives 15,000 calls/month, so (15,000 minus 1,000) times $35/1,000 is about $490/month. The Place Details mask includes 'reviews', an Enterprise + Atmosphere field, at $25/1,000 with 1,000 free. PLACE_DETAILS_DAILY_CAP=200 gives 6,000/month, so about $125/month. Geocoding at 200/day is 6,000/month, inside the 10,000 Essentials free tier, so $0. Total about $615/month at cap. Dropping rating/userRatingCount/priceLevel from the nearby mask moves it to Nearby Search Pro ($32/1,000, 5,000 free) — still about $320/month at that cap. To stay free the caps need to be roughly 150/day nearby (Pro) and 30/day details (Atmosphere), or the Places-content surface should move to Places UI Kit's 10,000 free Query calls.

findings.topic: Caching and storage rules — what data/store.js may persist
findings.detail: Master Google Maps Platform Terms of Service section 3.2.3, verbatim: "(a) No Scraping. Customer will not export, extract, or otherwise scrape Google Maps Content for use outside the Services. For example, Customer will not: (i) pre-fetch, index, store, reshare, or rehost Google Maps Content outside the services; (ii) bulk download Google Maps tiles, Street View images, geocodes, directions, distance matrix results, roads information, places information, elevation values, and time zone details; (iii) copy and save business names, addresses, or user reviews; or (iv) use Google Maps Content with text-to-speech services. (b) No Caching. Customer will not cache Google Maps Content except as expressly permitted under the Maps Service Specific Terms. (c) No Creating Content From Google Maps Content... (iv) use latitude/longitude values from the Places API as an input for point-in-polygon analysis... (vii) use Google Maps Content to improve machine learning and artificial intelligence models, including to train, test, validate or fine-tune the models." The Places API policies page states the place ID is exempt from the caching restrictions and may be stored indefinitely. Net rules for businessfind: savedPlaces may persist ONLY the place ID, plus lat/lng for at most 30 consecutive calendar days per 14.3 / 15.2. Business names, addresses, ratings, review text and review author details must not be written to data/*.json — re-fetch at render time. Also note 3.2.3(c)(iv) rules out using Places lat/lng for point-in-polygon work such as neighbourhood assignment.

findings.topic: Attribution requirements: reviews and the Google logo
findings.detail: Places API policies page: "You must always credit the author when displaying photos or reviews. Each photo and review includes an author attribution (author's avatar image, name, and profile link)." The author's avatar is the minimum when space is constrained; name and profile link should appear where space permits. Display context: "Places API results displayed on a map must be shown on a Google Map, with proper attribution including the Google logo and third-party data providers, if applicable" and "When displaying Places API data without a Google Map, you must include the Google logo, adhering to the provided style guidelines and attribution requirements." Google logo spec from the same page: minimum height 16dp, maximum 19dp, clear space 10dp left/right/top and 5dp bottom, legible against the background, never modified. For Places UI Kit the components render Google's own attribution and ToS 15.4 forbids removing, altering or obscuring it — do not restyle component internals or overlay them. These quotes came through a summarising fetch of a JS-rendered page; treat the dp figures as directionally right and re-read the page before writing a pixel spec.

findings.topic: All 12 hardcoded place type strings are VALID Table A types — no silent zero-results bug
findings.detail: Checked against developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/place-types. CATEGORY_TYPES in /Users/atharv/buisnessfind/server.js lines 43-56 maps to restaurant (Food and Drink), cafe (Food and Drink), supermarket (Shopping), shopping_mall (Shopping), clothing_store (Shopping), pharmacy (Health and Wellness), gym (Sports), beauty_salon (Services), atm (Finance), gas_station (Automotive), bakery (Food and Drink), bar (Food and Drink). All twelve are present in Table A, the set valid for searchNearby includedTypes. None are deprecated or renamed, and none carry the asterisk marking additions from the February 12, 2026 release. Optional free coverage improvements, all also Table A: coffee_shop alongside cafe, drugstore alongside pharmacy, fitness_center alongside gym, hair_salon and nail_salon alongside beauty_salon, grocery_store and convenience_store alongside supermarket. includedTypes takes an array and adding types to one request does not increase cost, but server.js currently passes a single-element array.

findings.topic: FieldMask syntax — the two endpoints differ, and server.js has both right
findings.detail: searchNearby (POST https://places.googleapis.com/v1/places:searchNearby): header X-Goog-FieldMask, every entry prefixed with 'places.', e.g. 'places.displayName,places.formattedAddress'. No spaces anywhere in the list. '*' returns all fields and is discouraged in production. Place Details (GET /v1/places/{PLACE_ID}): header X-Goog-FieldMask with NO 'places.' prefix, e.g. 'id,displayName'; a ?fields= query parameter is also accepted. server.js uses both forms correctly. Place Details SKU tiers by field — ESSENTIALS-IDs-only: attributions, consumerAlert, id, movedPlace, movedPlaceId, name, photos. ESSENTIALS: addressComponents, addressDescriptor, adrFormatAddress, formattedAddress, location, plusCode, postalAddress, shortFormattedAddress, types, viewport. PRO: accessibilityOptions, businessStatus, containingPlaces, displayName, googleMapsLinks, iconBackgroundColor, iconMaskBaseUri, primaryType, timeZone, utcOffsetMinutes. ENTERPRISE: currentOpeningHours, internationalPhoneNumber, nationalPhoneNumber, priceLevel, rating, regularOpeningHours, userRatingCount, websiteUri. ENTERPRISE + ATMOSPHERE: allowsDogs, delivery, dineIn, editorialSummary, evChargeOptions, generativeSummary, goodForChildren, liveMusic, neighborhoodSummary, parkingOptions, paymentOptions, reviews, reviewSummary, servesBeer, servesBreakfast, takeout and similar. Billing is by the highest tier any single requested field belongs to, applied to the whole request.

findings.topic: Which mask entries push you into the expensive Atmosphere tier
findings.detail: For Place Details, the single most expensive entry in server.js's mask is 'reviews' — it alone moves the call from Enterprise ($20/1,000) to Enterprise + Atmosphere ($25/1,000) and caps the free allowance at 1,000/month. 'editorialSummary', 'generativeSummary', 'reviewSummary' and the amenity booleans do the same. For searchNearby, 'places.reviews' is the Atmosphere trigger, while 'places.rating', 'places.userRatingCount', 'places.priceLevel', 'places.websiteUri' and the phone/hours fields are the Enterprise triggers. Note also that 'photos' is only an Essentials-tier mask field — it returns photo resource names, but actually fetching each image hits the separate Place Details Photos SKU at $7/1,000 with 1,000 free/month, so the current 6-photo gallery per detail view is 6 billable photo calls each time.

findings.topic: Architectural consequence: the server proxy and in-process daily caps do not survive a move to Places UI Kit
findings.detail: Places UI Kit is a client-side Maps JavaScript API web component loaded by script tag from maps.googleapis.com and used as custom elements. That is compatible with the zero-npm-dependency and no-build-step constraints (it is not an npm package), but it is NOT compatible with store.js's tryConsume/usageRemaining daily caps, because the calls originate in the browser with the browser key and never pass through the Node process. Cost control must move to Google Cloud Console: an HTTP-referrer-restricted browser key plus per-day and per-minute quota caps on the Places UI Kit SKUs. If the hard in-process daily cap is a locked requirement, the UI Kit path conflicts with it and the app must keep the server proxy and use a Google map instead.

recommendation:
Pick one of two coherent architectures — the current half-and-half plan is both a terms violation and roughly $615/month at the configured caps.

OPTION A (recommended for cost and for reviews): use Places UI Kit for all Google content. Render the business list, place detail panel and reviews with Places UI Kit web components (Place Search Element, Place Details Element). ToS 15.1 explicitly permits this on any map including MapLibre/Leaflet and states it prevails over the 14.2 non-Google-map ban. Billing is flat per component instantiation regardless of fields, so reviews, photos and hours are free extras, at 10,000 free Query calls/month then $1.00/1,000 — roughly 30x cheaper than the current Enterprise Nearby Search path. Trade-offs: card visuals are Google's, so the user-selectable themes feature can only theme the chrome around the components (15.4 forbids obscuring their attribution), and the hard daily caps must move from store.js into Cloud Console quota caps because these calls bypass the Node server.

OPTION B (keeps the current server.js design): use the Google Maps JavaScript API dynamic map (10,000 free loads/month, then $7/1,000) as the only map, keep the server proxy and in-process caps, and cut the field masks hard — drop places.rating, places.userRatingCount and places.priceLevel from searchNearby to land on the Pro SKU. Reviews still bill at Enterprise + Atmosphere on Place Details. Set NEARBY_DAILY_CAP to about 150 (5,000 Pro free calls/month) and PLACE_DETAILS_DAILY_CAP to about 30 (1,000 Atmosphere free calls/month) for a $0 bill. Themes then means Google map styling, which is fine.

Do NOT ship the current plan: raw /api/nearby and /api/place JSON rendered onto a MapLibre or Leaflet map breaches Service Specific Terms 14.2.

Three changes are non-negotiable in either option. (1) /Users/atharv/buisnessfind/data/store.js savedPlaces must persist only the place ID — place IDs are exempt from caching limits, but names, addresses, ratings and review text fall under ToS 3.2.3(a)(iii) "copy and save business names, addresses, or user reviews"; any cached lat/lng needs a 30-day expiry per 14.3. (2) Every review must carry author attribution — avatar, name, profile link — and the Google logo must appear wherever Places data is shown, 16-19dp tall and unmodified. (3) The 12 includedTypes strings are all valid so no fix is required, but widening each to an array (cafe + coffee_shop, pharmacy + drugstore, gym + fitness_center, beauty_salon + hair_salon + nail_salon, supermarket + grocery_store + convenience_store) costs nothing per request and materially improves results in Indian cities.

Unrelated but boot-blocking: /Users/atharv/buisnessfind/server.js requires ./seo-content.js for { seoPages, categoryList } and that file does not exist, and public/ is empty.
